x: Collis passed in 29mins., Gebbett 29.35 Bishop and McDonald 30.53, Jordan 31.15, Plummer 32.55 and Penstone 33.10. At 10 miles Colin was noticeably pegging back the stragglers of the leading bunch, whilst Eric was running easily with Fowle, Ash, Meckler, Braughton & Co.
McDonald, just sufficient for a team, set off on the long run to Brighton. Bill Wortley, the fastest of the three, ran in fifth position in a field of 40 for the first 20 miles.
C = No. of times carded during season but failed to turn up. S = Star rating - ranging from 10 for McDonald, McMillan, Glover,etc. to 0 for Pearson O'Connor and North.

Once off, however, they tore down the Embankment like the wind, and as the field reached the coloured lights of Albert Bridge, twinklingly reflected in the dark Thames below, our Belgrave heroes - McDonald, Plummer, 'Boofer' Bruce, etc. - could be seen bounding along like young gazelles.

By the time they ended the first circuit just Coughlan and Ranelagh's McDonald were in contention and then up the steep Victoria Drive for the second time our Kiwi pulled away to gain a winning advantage of well over a minute by the finish. 1, P.Coughlan 53:22; 3, K.Quinn 55:02.
